findings.rationale: The declared idempotency_key is only syntax-validated. Effect status, attempt counters, admission guards, and writes are all keyed solely by correlation_id. Reusing one idempotency key with different correlations can therefore launch the effect repeatedly, while distinct idempotency keys sharing a correlation incorrectly collide.

The request-producing command excludes only Pending and Succeeded, so it is enabled again after Failed or TimedOut and resets attempts to 1. Re-entering through that command avoids the retry action's attempts < maximum guard, permitting unlimited effect executions despite max_attempts.

Await guards are generated only when step.emits is empty. A step containing both emits and awaits therefore ignores every awaited event; its normal and timeout actions use the same remaining guards and no progress state, allowing premature, repeated, or conflicting transitions.

Every action rewrites every event flag, clearing events not emitted by that same transition. An awaits_mode=all guard conjuncts those transient flags, so events observed in separate transitions never accumulate and the step cannot advance unless one action happens to emit all awaited events simultaneously.

after_event is validated and embedded in the action name but never included in the compensation guard or retained as progress state. The compensation can execute on trigger_event before the declared after_event has occurred.

The text renderer accepts any rendered correlation expression, extracts its final dotted component, and looks up that field on the request event; failure merely suppresses effect state and actions. Direct lowering instead requires Event.field and resolves the qualifier's event. Missing, malformed, or differently qualified correlations can thus be rejected by one path but silently produce an executable model with the effect lifecycle omitted or differently typed in the other.
